items.requirement: Record screen: robust target suggestions for each recorded action, user-selectable.
items.evidence: L4.8 parts 1–2 (capture + draft; the Record screen is parts 3–5): kit 1.6.0 (packages/runner-web/src/kit/kit.ts) `inventory({alternatives})` / `suggestFor(el, {alternatives})` go on along the target ladder past the verified suggestion — never `nth` / `last_visible`, never a key the indexes know is shared, each verified to resolve once to the same element, at most 3 kept and 6 extra verifications, an own in-page budget of min(10 ms, what is left of the press's 150 ms), skipped (`alternatives_partial`) after a suggestion over 20 ms or on a page of over 2,000 distinct texts; page_inspect's inventory never carries them. The recorder (kit/record-script.ts `info(target, alts)`) asks for them on a press, a keyboard activation, typing, a native select and a file, never for a secret field; they go through the runner's secret masking and core `RecordedElementSchema.alternatives` (≤ 3, never positional). Core `recordedAlternatives(el)` lists the offered ones (masked, templated or same-as-suggestion dropped) and `draftFromRecording(events, ctx, annotations)` applies a pick (studio.json `choices`, core record-annotations.ts) only when emitting: every fold compares the recorded targets, the latest of a step's target events with a choice wins, the recorder's own wait_for / scroll before the action follow it; `sources[].target_seq` says where a step's alternatives are picked. Cost on the lab: a press p50 1 ms / p95 4 ms in the page with alternatives, the same without (headless, 2026-10-28). Tests: packages/core/test/recording.test.ts (42: every L3.4 case run three ways — as is, with alternatives on every element incl. masked / templated ones, with empty annotations — gives the same draft and issue codes; 'packages/core/test/recording.test.ts > draftFromRecording: target picks (L4.8) > a pick on the press before the typing arrives, then the typing: still one step, the pick follows into `type {into}`'), packages/core/test/record-annotations.test.ts (6), packages/runner-web/test/kit-suggest.test.ts (7: alternatives verified in the page, a key shared with a non-interactive element not offered, a spent budget → none and partial), packages/runner-web/test/record-alternatives.test.ts (3: each alternative re-checked in the window to resolve once to the pressed element, none for a secret field, none and partial with a 0 ms budget, the in-page cost); the L3.4 recorder tests unchanged and green (runner-web record-session 20, engine record 10 and record-jobs 8, cli record 3, mcp stdio-record 4). Mutation-checked: a masked alternative changing an issue code, a pick swapped before the build (splits the fold), the earliest pick winning, helpers not following, an alternative kept without verification, a secret field given alternatives. Part 3: engine `record.view` lists each step's offered alternatives (`untrusted.alternatives`: index 0 the suggestion, words, fragile) and `record.annotate {op: choose}` stores a pick under the lock and revision; the saved scenario carries it ('packages/engine/test/record-studio.test.ts > a Studio recording: live view, annotations, Stop, Save > records the lab: meta.json, no auto-save, a caption at the end after a Studio visit, a hold, a pick, Stop runs the check'). L4.8 part 4 (Studio server): record_view gives each step's alternatives (`untrusted.alternatives`: options in words, the chosen index) and record_annotate `choose {seq, index}` at the view's revision (strict input, no author / submitted_by). 'packages/ui/test/record-ops.test.ts > the allow-list and the pinned inputs > record_view / annotate / stop / discard / save: ids never paths, no author or submitted_by, strict changes'. The viewer's frames: `renders.frame` / `renders.outline` (engine render-frames.ts) — an input seek to (F − 0.5)/fps, the video's own fps and frame count (ffprobe of the open descriptor) checked against the record (a record whose fps is not its video's is refused; frames bounded by min(record.frames, plan.durationInFrames, the video's frames)); `renders/<id>.mp4` built from the id, the record's file resolving to it, O_NOFOLLOW, one name, checked once open, descriptors only; a 32 MB memory LRU, the engine's 2 ffmpeg slots shared with the run thumbnails, ≤ 4 requests waiting or running (else busy), newest wins per session and render, 15 s timeout. items.requirement: Local engine API (HTTP/JSON + event stream: progress, logs, live preview frames) shared by the Studio UI, the MCP server and the CLI; the UI never reads workspace files directly.
items.evidence: L3.1: the engine is one typed, in-process API (@retake/engine createEngine: projects, scenarios, runs, jobs, hooks, env, auth, sandbox, usage) shared by the CLI (moved functions, native errors) and the MCP server; progress as job events (events.jsonl) and MCP progress notifications. The ADR-1 amendment (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) separates where the engine runs from how a UI reaches it. L4.1 part 1: the engine's local HTTP/JSON API (engine src/http/: the gate in a fixed order Host → Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site → route / method → token → content type / size, the 127.0.0.1 listener, tokens and one-time bootstrap codes, the discovery file, ERROR_STATUS) served by `retake ui` (packages/ui): GET /v1/info, POST /v1/session, POST /v1/bootstrap, POST /v1/call/<op> for an allow-list of the MCP tools; the page reads no file (static assets from memory, data through /v1). Tests: packages/engine/test/http-gate.test.ts (each layer with a valid token over raw requests; all mutation-checked), packages/engine/test/http-discovery.test.ts, packages/ui/test/server.test.ts. L4.1 part 3: the event stream — GET /v1/events (server-sent events read through fetch, the token in a header): hello, workspace {projects, readme}, jobs {changed}, index {generation}; at most 4 streams, one per browser (packages/ui/src/server/live.ts, src/app/events.ts). Tests: 'packages/ui/test/events.test.ts > /v1/events > the gate first: no token 401, another page 403 even with the token, GET only', 'packages/ui/test/events.test.ts > /v1/events > at most 4 streams (EVENT_STREAMS_MAX): the next one 503 too_many_streams; a closed one frees its slot'. L4.4 part B: POST /v1/live — the run's progress as a stream (a reduced view of log.jsonl and the job's notes, byte-offset cursors) and its live preview frames relayed from the worker's channel. Tests: 'packages/ui/test/run-live.test.ts > POST /v1/live: steps and log from log.jsonl > snapshot then progress with byte-offset seq; after resumes without a duplicate; job notes merged; long lines skipped; end', 'packages/ui/test/run-live.test.ts > POST /v1/live: the live picture > a dry run: the upstream opens only while a page stream wants frames, ONE per job, and closes when none does; frames relayed as sent'.
items.gap: The scenario screen still re-reads run_status on `jobs` / `workspace` events (ids) — the Run screen (part C) follows the stream; other jobs (render, record, inspect) report progress as `jobs` events only.

items.requirement: Job runner abstraction (capture, render, review, export: status, progress, cancel) executed by a local worker, designed so a remote worker can be added later without changing callers.
items.evidence: L3.1 part B: a job queue of files under <workspace>/.retake/jobs/<id>/ (packages/engine/src/jobs/queue.ts: job.json written once by the submitter then only by the claiming worker, O_EXCL claim and cancel marker files, events.jsonl, `interrupted` / cancelled-before-start derived when reading) with a zod-validated, serialisable input contract (core jobs.ts JobInputSchema: slugs, names, the scenario's sha256, a reserved run id — never secrets or absolute paths), executed by a detached local worker (jobs/worker.ts, worker-main.ts, hidden `retake worker`): one per workspace through worker.lock (pid + start time + build), one job at a time, status / progress / cancel. Callers only see engine.runs.submit / engine.jobs.* (the queue is an interface a remote control plane can implement later). Tests: packages/engine/test/jobs.test.ts, packages/engine/test/worker-process.test.ts (claim, cancel queued and running, SIGTERM, SIGKILL → interrupted, two workers, a second signal, the workspace gone). Parts C/D: kinds hooks, env_reset, auth_login, sandbox_up, sandbox_reset; the worker's dispatch is an exhaustive switch over the kinds (packages/engine/src/jobs/worker.ts); each finished (or interrupted) job is appended to <workspace>/.retake/history.jsonl; `retake jobs` list / status / cancel (packages/cli/test/jobs.test.ts). L3.2 part A: kind `render` (engine jobs/render-job.ts; Remotion imported lazily by the worker; the render browser's pid + start time recorded in the job folder and killed by the next worker after a SIGKILL; history counts a render once written: packages/engine/test/render-jobs.test.ts, render-worker-process.test.ts). L3.1 review fixes: the build stamp covers the engine and every @retake package it depends on at run time, transitively from the package.json files (hooks included; engine jobs/build.ts buildDirs; test agent-safety.test.ts 'build stamp'); a worker refuses (failed, invalid, 'refused without running') a job whose input version or kind it does not know, and leaves it to a worker of the new build when its code changed (worker-process.test.ts 'a job of a kind or input version it does not know …'); approvals are signed and verified (jobs/signing.ts); `retake jobs` (client cli) never starts a worker (packages/cli/test/jobs.test.ts: no worker.log after a cancel, the run listed cancelled); `retake still` and the formats `retake export` re-renders are counted in history.jsonl. L3.2 part B: kinds `review` and `export` (engine jobs/review-job.ts, export-job.ts; the review package and the editor imported lazily; status / progress with `fraction` / cancel: a review checks its signal between stages and kills ffmpeg, keeping the previous review — its swap sets the old one aside first and recoverReviewDir brings it back after a crash —, an export stops between formats; after a SIGKILL the next worker restores the review folder or kills an export re-render's browser and removes partial files: packages/engine/test/review-export-jobs.test.ts, render-worker-process.test.ts). The four job kinds of the requirement (capture, render, review, export) run through the same queue and worker. L5.14a: two slots per worker (captures first: a capture in the worker, a heavy job in a job process of its own, `worker-main --job`), R-CAP-01…05.
items.gap: No remote worker (BL-05/06): the ADR-1 amendment fixes the job input contract it would read.

items.requirement: Media storage abstraction for artefacts (local paths now, object storage later), content-hashed where useful.
items.evidence: packages/engine/src/storage.ts: Storage interface + LocalStorage(projectDir) — refs are project-relative POSIX paths (checkRef refuses absolute, '..', '.', empty segments, backslashes), resolve / refOf, describe (stat + streamed sha256), readText → {text, sha256}, writeText with if_match (atomic temp + rename, link() for must-not-exist, symlink escape refused by comparing real paths). Used by scenario_save, project_update_readme, run_status outputs ({ref, path, sha256} once finished) and sandbox_status refs. Tests: packages/engine/test/engine.test.ts 'maps refs to paths and back, refusing absolute paths, ".." and backslashes', 'writeText: …'.
items.gap: Local only, by design (object storage later). The runner, editor and review still write absolute paths into run.json / render.json: refs there are a format change (L3.6 / BL-70); no put / list / hash cache yet (L3.2 exports).

items.requirement: Frame comments stored one file per thread (<project>/comments/<scenario>/<thread-id>.json) to avoid conflicts.
items.evidence: See R-CMT-02: one file per thread written by the engine store (packages/engine/src/comments.ts, L3.6 part 2), entries appended under a per-thread lock.

items.requirement: SQLite index under <workspace>/.retake/ (runs, renders, jobs, search) rebuilt from files; files stay the source of truth.
items.evidence: L4.1 part 3: engine src/index-db/ — WorkspaceIndex over node:sqlite at <workspace>/.retake/index.sqlite (WAL, timeout 2000): projects (name, error, README text), runs (run.json via listRuns), renders (renders/*.json read as data), the job history (history.jsonl, read from its last whole line; a shorter file or another inode read again) and an FTS5 search over them, rebuilt from the files and reconciled by a bounded stat poll (sources.ts: a few stats per project, the run.json of unfinished runs; no fs.watch); missing → built, corrupt (quick_check, or errcode 11 / 26) or another schema → deleted with -wal / -shm and rebuilt; the files stay the only source of truth (every write goes to files through the engine; only the Studio server writes the index). Jobs: finished ones are history rows; unfinished ones are never read from the index (critique B2) — activity() derives them live from the queue. Node 22.0–22.12 (no node:sqlite) run without it (activity / search answer unavailable). Tests: 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > builds from the files: projects, README, scenarios, runs, renders, history; search by prefix words', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > reconciles what changed only: a README edit, a new run, a removed project', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > history.jsonl: appended lines only, a torn last line waits, a truncated or replaced file is read again', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > rebuilt when garbage, truncated or of another schema (its -wal and -shm with it); reused otherwise', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > a Node.js without node:sqlite: no index (null), nothing written', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > the loader swallows only the experimental notice of node:sqlite, matched by its message (B11)', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > a search query never carries FTS syntax: quoted prefix terms, bound as a parameter', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the activity feed and the job watch (critique B2) > unfinished jobs live from the queue — a SIGKILLed worker reads interrupted at once — then history, newest first'; the built `retake ui` prints nothing on stderr on Node 22.16 with the index open (packages/cli/test/ui.test.ts). Mutation-checked (11 mutations of the index, each failing a test: corruption by errcode, quick_check, schema check, history offset, history reset, torn line, unfinished run.json, FTS quoting, warning filter removed / by type, activity without derived states). L4.1 fixes (review A L3, L4; review B L1): a README or render record is indexed only as a regular file within a cap, inside the project once links are followed (a link out of renders/ or a FIFO is never opened), run.json only as a regular file (also for run_list / run_status); an index.sqlite, -wal or -shm that is a symbolic link is removed and the index rebuilt (`not_a_file`), its target never created; activity() reads a finished job's file once (3,000 finished jobs: 214 ms the first call, 7 ms after — before: ≈ 190 ms every call). Tests: 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > an index file (or its -wal) that is a symbolic link is removed and rebuilt, never followed: the target is never created (review A L4)', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the workspace index > render records, run records and READMEs linked out of the project are never indexed; a FIFO is never opened (review A L3)', 'packages/engine/test/index-db.test.ts > the activity feed reads a finished job once (review B L1) > a second call reads only the files of unfinished jobs'; mutation-checked.

items.requirement: Cloud layer (later, not V1): shareable review links with comments, team sync, optional cloud render. No browser extension.
Environment pages accept {url, display}: the runner navigates the real URL; timeline keeps both; browser layout, review and captions show only the display URL (never localhost in a video).
items.evidence: Data side (L1.7 part 1): pages are a URL or {url, display} in both environment forms (schemas/project.ts PageValueSchema, display validated by core displayError); loadProject keeps the real URLs in ProjectConfig.environments and the normalised display bases in environment_settings (core env.ts normalizeEnvironments); the runner navigates the real URL and writes the display table to timeline.json environment.display (runner-web run.ts timelineEnvironment; test 'timeline.environment holds the access, the display table and the clock' in runner-web/test/access.test.ts); pure mapping helpers displayTable / displayUrl / isLocalHost / findLocalUrls (core display.ts; core/test/environments.test.ts 'display URLs'). Edit side (L1.7 part 3): core displayPages + templateSceneEntry(entry, i, ctx, editCtx) (interpolateAt ctxAt) — the text the video shows (captions, cards, overlays, page labels, title, intro, outro) reads `{{page}}` as the display URL, steps / `open` / hooks / mocks keep the real one (runner Runtime.editTemplate, run.ts templateVideo; core/test/scenario-template.test.ts 'display URLs in edit text'). The planner maps every browser-bar URL through timeline.environment.display; a URL still local is kept `hidden` (urlAt / paneUrlAt skip it: the bar shows no address, window bars fall back to the theme's brand.url) and warned about once per page only where the layout draws a URL (editor drawsUrl: studio/layout-browser unless show_url and tabs are both off, split / pip with `chrome`, the pip's main page only); a notification overlay's app is the display host (a local one without display: the theme's brand name). Tests: editor planner-geometry (display URLs, hidden + warning, show_url false, tabs), planner-panes (split bars with and without the table, motion warnings, pip drawsUrl), planner-artefacts (notification app); review checks.test 'environment (L1.7)' (url-hidden only on URL-drawing layouts, local-url-text), tutorial.test (tutorial-stale-target names the display URL or the local path). Fixture project: display URLs console / shop.northfield.example on local, signed-in and production. Mac: read-only-v3 (run 20261013-185847-read-only, browser frame) shows `shop.northfield.example`, `…/products/selowa-ridge`, `…/quotes` with the lock and the caption 'Live prices at https://shop.northfield.example, …'; its report.md / report.json / review timeline.json and the raw export of the run (validate-raw OK) contain no 'localhost'; quote on env local rendered --frame browser (quote-v3): display URLs in the bar, review clean; live-quote --theme motion (live-quote-v3): split window bars shop.northfield.example / console.northfield.example; an older quote run without a display table (20261012-211729-quote → quote-v4, browser): empty bar, one plan warning and 4 url-hidden warnings naming paths only. Review fixes (display / review pass): display URLs are edit-time data — core editDisplayTable puts project.yaml's current pages of the run's environment (timeline.environment.name, else run.json `env`: PlanEditInput.env, passed by render / plan / still) over the table the run recorded; the edit's table is plan.display and the review names URLs through it (editor planner-geometry 'display URLs are edit-time data…', review checks.test 'url-hidden…'); the plan warning names the page and says to render again. core displayUrl maps http(s) only (blob: / filesystem: the URL they wrap; file: local, hidden), a page without a display URL claims its URLs (displayRows: longest prefix over every page; the origin fallback only for URLs no page claims); isLocalHost adds dotless names, *.lan, *.home.arpa and kin, 100.64/10, IPv4-mapped IPv6 and written forms (127.1, 2130706433); findLocalUrls finds bare host:port and host/path (shop.localhost:4402, app.test:3000/x, [::1]:4402, localhost/admin; never 16:9); displayError refuses a local display host and an invalid port (core/test/environments.test.ts 'display URLs'). Findings never name a local host: every local URL of a plan warning is masked, local-url-text names paths, a file: URL its file name (review checks.test, review.test 'a report never names a local host…'); raw export step markers and click targets name the display URL or the path (runner-web exportDisplayTable / shownTargets, raw-units 'URLs in the package'); an overlay's target is templated with the real URL, its slots with the display one (core scenario-template.test). Mac (review pass): takes 20261013-205843-read-only / 20261013-205930-read-only rendered read-only-v4 (browser frame): the bar shows shop.northfield.example, review clean, no 'localhost' in report.md / report.json / the review's timeline.json, nor in the raw export of the take (markers, manifest, README, cursor data; the render record's plan.display keeps the real bases, like timeline.json); the reviewer's probe run re-exported: step marker '2. open https://shop.northfield.example/products/selowa-ridge' (was the localhost URL). The run 20261012-211729-quote (captured before L1.7, no environment block) re-rendered --frame browser (quote-v6): shop.northfield.example/… in the bar on every clip, no plan warning, review clean, no 'localhost' in its report. env local quote (20261013-210124 → quote-v5) and catalogue (20261013-210328 → catalogue-v3): reviews clean, the same known ripple warnings as before.
items.gap: Captured content is filmed as it is (the page's own text and links, captured email HTML and PDFs): BACKLOG BL-63.

items.requirement: Environment flags `production: true` and `access: read-only | read-write` (read-only by default in production).
items.evidence: project.yaml environments: short form unchanged, long form {production, access, pages, read_only} (keyed union on `pages`, schemas/project.ts; settings written in the short form get one targeted error, a page key named like a setting with a URL stays a page); core environmentAccess (read-only by default in production) and resolveRunAccess / runAccess (the matrix of docs/DESIGN.md §1: production + access: read-write is read-only with a notice unless --allow-writes; the flag on a read-only environment is AccessError → CLI usage error); ResolvedEnvironment carries production / access / display / read_only. Tests: core/test/environments.test.ts ('project.yaml environments…', 'access of a run'), schema.test.ts (JSON schema $defs.Environment), cli/test/read-only.test.ts.

items.requirement: Read-only enforcement by request interception in the browser context: mutating requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, GraphQL mutations) to the environment hosts are blocked except allow-listed patterns; a blocked request either fails or is answered by a configured mock so the flow continues on screen.
items.evidence: Configuration and classifier (L1.7 part 1): read_only.hosts / allow / mocks in the long form and scenario `mocks` (schemas, validation: patterns parsed, GET patterns refused, page keys of the environment, mocks literal, json xor body; warnings for read_only on a read-write environment and for mocks on a read-write scenario environment); core writes.ts: isWriteMethod, minimal GraphQL (graphqlOf: queries sent as POST read, mutations and persisted queries write), request patterns (page:/path, /path, * and **), compileWritePolicy (guarded hosts = pages' hosts + read_only.hosts, scenario mocks first) and classifyRequest (blocked / mocked / allowed / passed) — core/test/environments.test.ts 'request patterns and the write classifier'. Browser guard (L1.7 part 2, runner-web write-guard.ts): every persona browser of a read-only run armed at launch, before the preflight's check page (context.route + an init script + a WebSocket warning; a browser launched later too); per request: reads at once, then core classifyRequest — mocked → route.fulfill (status, JSON, delay_ms), allowed / passed (unguarded host) → through, blocked → a navigation in any frame answered 204 (the page stays), anything else aborted; a request without a resolvable frame (popup, new window, service worker) is guarded; the automated sign-in tab is exempt (recorded via sign-in), js hook tabs are guarded by their own tab (writes stopped, never mocked: WriteRefusedError → refused); service workers' own requests reach the route (Playwright's service-worker network events); writes sent while a page unloads are stopped (pages closed through about:blank + keepalive / sendBeacon to guarded hosts turned into ordinary requests — each measure alone leaks, measured); watchNavigation drops a navigation answered 204 / aborted at once (a stopped form submit: click 15.3 s → under 2 s); every write recorded in timeline.environment.writes (capture time, outcome, rule, via) with one run warning per stopped request and per unguarded host. Tests: runner-web/test/write-guard.test.ts (12 real-browser tests, every write reaching the server counted: fetch / XHR / dedicated worker / popup / cross-site frame, form POST in the main frame, an iframe and a new window, mocks / allow / GraphQL query, mutation and persisted queries, unload writes on a navigation, a closed tab and a closed session ×3, a service worker answering the page and in the background, two persona browsers and a later one, a js hook tab, a read-only run with a document tab fetched by context.request), runner-web/test/auth.test.ts (the automated sign-in's POST passes, the app's own POST /expire is stopped, the session survives), cli/test/read-only.test.ts (a js hook writing on production is refused). Fixture capture (scratch; quote until `delivery`, environment local made production in memory, hooks skipped, POST shop:/api/quotes mocked 201 {id, supplier}): succeeded, the toast 'Quote request sent … Northfield Roasters usually replies within a few hours' on camera, writes = [mocked page POST /api/quotes at 30.8 s], no quote reached the fixture; reports read-only: held loads 228/162/1365/108/1357 ms vs 297/173/1365/105/1361 ms read-write (the route's disabled HTTP cache costs nothing locally). Fixture and e2e (part 3): `/api/health` counts `mutations` (successful non-GET API calls since the server started, never reset); environment `production` of the fixture project (the local fixture, read-only, an environment-level mock for POST shop:/api/notifications/read) and scenario `read-only` (scenario mock POST shop:/api/quotes 201 {id, supplier}, delay 300 ms). cli/test/read-only-fixture.test.ts: a dry run of the committed scenario (quick pacing) records one mocked page write, no warning, `mutations` unchanged. Mac: two takes 20261013-185800-read-only / 20261013-185847-read-only (41.4 s each): writes = [mocked POST /api/quotes at 31.6 s], none stopped, the toast 'Quote request sent … Northfield Roasters usually replies within a few hours' on camera, the quotes list unchanged (Q-1042 first); `mutations` 0 → 0 across both; after a POST /api/reset (1), a dry read-only run with its setup hook: 1 → 1. Run summary: 'writes 1 mocked, 0 stopped (read-only)'. Review fixes (safety pass): a production environment guards every host (fail closed: core compileWritePolicy hosts ["*"]; a write anywhere needs an allow entry or a mock), a non-production read-only one keeps its pages' hosts + read_only.hosts and the `passed` warning; read_only.hosts entries are validated (core hostPatternError: no path, no leading dot; an IDN matched in punycode); an allow / mock entry narrowed to a GraphQL operation covers a body only when every write operation of it (batches included, anonymous mutations and persisted queries counted) is that one; a JSON body is GraphQL only with keys query / operationName / variables / extensions and a `query` that is a document (POST {name, query: '{"status":"open"}'} writes) — core/test/environments.test.ts ('compiles the guarded hosts…', the batch / JSON rows of the classifier table, 'a read-only environment that is not production…', 'read_only.hosts entries are host patterns…'). `fetchLater` (sent past the route on the next navigation, a closed tab, session close or its timer: probe 3 of 3 leaked) and `SharedWorker` (Playwright detaches from shared workers: its POST reached the server from a guarded page and from a js hook tab) are deleted from every frame and popup of a guarded browser and of every js hook tab (write-guard.ts UNGUARDED_APIS_SCRIPT). The automated sign-in tab is exempt only while its main frame is on its persona's sign-in page (recorded `exempt`): the page it lands on is guarded (probe: PUT /api/last-seen and POST /api/onboarding/complete reached production before, now stopped, recorded `via: sign-in` and counted), and it bypasses service workers (a worker forwarding its sign-in POST no longer fails the login). Tests: runner-web/test/write-guard.test.ts ('fetchLater and SharedWorker do not exist in a guarded page…', 'js hook tabs never have fetchLater nor SharedWorker… on a read-write run too', 'the automated sign-in tab: exempt on its sign-in page only…' ×2 — every write reaching the server counted), runner-web/test/auth.test.ts (a run whose sign-in lands on a page that writes: the sign-in POST passes, the landing page's fetch and beacon are stopped, nothing reaches the server).
items.gap: Not inspected by design (README limits, BACKLOG BL-64): WebSocket / WebTransport messages (warned per host), unsafe GETs, a write to an unguarded host that redirects to a guarded one (its first hop is recorded `passed`). fetchLater and SharedWorker do not exist in a guarded browser (an app that requires them, rather than feature-detecting them, fails on a guarded run).

items.requirement: Writing hooks are refused on read-only environments; writing in production needs `access: read-write` in the project AND `--allow-writes` at run time (explicit confirmation in the Studio app); run.json/timeline record the access mode and review shows it.
items.evidence: Hooks (L1.7 part 1): a read-only run refuses a hook that writes after templating, before anything runs (HookSecurityError reason read-only, status refused, never tolerated by optional, dry runs report it): http by method (GraphQL queries read), sql by core sqlWriteStatement (+ BEGIN READ ONLY), shell unless `writes: false`, a setup hook whose rollback writes; journal replays judge each entry by its own environment (ctx.accessOf) — hooks/test/read-only.test.ts. js hooks (part 2): their tab stops their writes at request level, never mocked; a hook that fails after a stopped write is refused (core WriteRefusedError → HookSecurityError read-only), one that catches it goes on with a warning — runner-web/test/write-guard.test.ts ('js hook tabs…', 'a js setup hook whose write is stopped is refused'), hooks/test/read-only.test.ts, cli/test/read-only.test.ts ('js hooks on read-only environments'). --allow-writes on retake run / hooks run / hooks rollback / env reset (usage error on a read-only environment; production + access: read-write runs read-only with a notice without it). retake run refuses a read-only run with writing hooks before any browser opens, secret is read or hook runs (runner-web/test/access.test.ts with an unusable browser executable; cli/test/read-only.test.ts). run.json environment {production, access, clock} + options.allow_writes, timeline.json environment {name, production, access, allow_writes, display, clock, writes}; secrets policy keeps them (runner-web/test/secrets.test.ts). Run header prints production / read-only / writes allowed / clock. Review (part 3): ReviewResult.environment and the report.md line 'Environment production · production · read-only · 1 write mocked · clock 2026-11-02T10:24:00' (also printed by retake review / render --review); findings `write-blocked` (one per method and path, at its output frame), `url-hidden`, `local-url-text` (review checks.test.ts 'environment (L1.7)', review.test.ts). The run summary counts a read-only run's writes (cli writesSummary, cli/test/read-only-fixture.test.ts). Mac: read-only-v3 review clean with the environment line; `retake run northfield-fixture quote --env production` refused before the browser opens (its 3 writing hooks listed); `retake hooks run northfield-fixture reset --env production` refused; `read-only --allow-writes` is a usage error. Review fixes (safety pass): no run writes to another environment's hosts — core crossEnvironmentHosts: the pages' hosts and read_only.hosts of every environment the run would be read-only on (production unless access: read-write and --allow-writes; access: read-only), minus the page hosts of the environments it may write to (the fixture's production shares localhost with local: nothing protected, nothing armed); a hook that writes to one is refused in any run (http by its URL and every writing redirect hop, sql by its database host, shell by the hosts it names: PreparedHook.hosts → checkWriteHosts, reason read-only; js by its tab: WriteRefusedError protectedBy), and the browser of a read-write run stops writes to them (no mock, no allow; recorded protected_by, summary '1 stopped (hosts of read-only environments)'). Probe: a teardown http POST {{vars.prod_api}}/api/reset on env local reached production before, now refused. SQL: a quoted identifier counts by its name (SET "transaction_read_only" = off, RESET, SET "role", "nextval"(…) now write) and dblink / dblink_exec write. items.requirement: Snapshot reset: a database snapshot taken after seeding is restored before each take (faster than reseeding), with a documented Postgres recipe.
items.evidence: L1.8 part C (packages/sandbox src/snapshot-postgres.ts, Sandbox.resetLocked): reset.strategy snapshot (docker-compose) — after the seed the database (reset.snapshot.database, default the first) is copied as <db>__ds_snapshot (ALTER … ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false, its backends terminated, the old template dropped, CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE <db> with STRATEGY left to the server, connections back in a finally, the template marked ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false IS_TEMPLATE true and COMMENT 'retake snapshot <seed hash>'); each reset restores it (ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false, DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS … WITH (FORCE), CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE … OWNER <owner at the take>, no abort check between DROP and CREATE). Every reset first repairs ALLOW_CONNECTIONS and recreates a database an interrupted restore dropped. Refused unless the database's port is published by a running service of the sandbox's own compose project with no other listener (provider.publishedBy) and Postgres ≥ 13. Stale → seed + retake: the seed hash (core seedHash + the compose services' image ids) differs from the state's or the template's comment, the template is gone (down --volumes), or `reset --reseed`. Documented in README "Snapshot reset (Postgres)": the SQL, ownership, permissions, staleness, what a restore keeps (not ALTER DATABASE … SET), the app's pools (node-postgres needs a Pool 'error' handler; reset.restart), seeds that start from a clean state, plain pg_dump files → pg_dump --inserts or an exec seed (psql -f in the db container). Measured on this Mac (Postgres 17 in OrbStack, the init scaffold; times logged, never asserted): 5-row seed 20–30 ms vs restore 40–313 ms; with 600 000 rows + 2 indexes (114 MB) the seed takes 1.3–1.9 s (strategy reseed: 1.5–2.1 s resets) and the snapshot restores in 230–300 ms (first after a take 741 ms): 0.51–0.60 s resets; a take costs 0.45–0.74 s. Tests: sandbox/test/compose.test.ts (gated, RETAKE_TEST_DOCKER=1): up seeds + takes, a mutation undone by reset (restored, sequence back), --reseed retakes, prepareTake with the snapshot strategy (restored, 6 rows), a seed file change makes it stale (retaken, the template's comment = the new hash, IS_TEMPLATE true, no connections) — logged: up 6.8 s, seed 116 ms, take 32 ms, reset 3.6 s with reset.restart (restore 673 ms), --reseed 3.4 s, prepareTake 3.2 s (restore 323 ms); compose-units.test.ts (ownership refusals, quoting, target). Mac: run 20261014-000033-placeholder with --sandbox restored the snapshot in 275 ms (see R-SBX-02). — L1.8 review fixes: snapshotTarget and waitDatabases read where pg connects with pg's own parser (pgEndpoint → hooks sandboxDatabaseProblem: a host / port parameter, a unix socket or a non-loopback host refused) and give pg.Client host / port / database / user / password explicitly, never the URL; a sql hook on a sandbox refuses the same; up waits for the server only — SQLSTATE 3D000 / 55000 count as ready — and resets a snapshot sandbox whose database an interrupted reset dropped or closed even when its seed is current; exec seed steps check the hosts of their rendered command and env at run time like shell hooks (compose services, allowed hosts, never a production host), mask their output in seed.log and errors, carry RETAKE_EXEC=<token> so Ctrl-C or the timeout stops their processes inside the container (sh + /proc; else a warning naming `docker compose restart`), and an interrupt stays exit 130. Tests: compose-units.test.ts (+3 and the exec test extended: hosts, masking, kill on abort / timeout), compose.test.ts (+2 gated: DROP DATABASE → up restores it (the whole test 13 s); ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false → up and prepareTake repair and restore; two `sleep` processes of an exec step gone after Ctrl-C and after a 2 s timeout — mutation-checked) — RETAKE_TEST_DOCKER=1: compose.test.ts 5/5 (57 s), cli/test/sandbox-docker.test.ts 1/1 (12 s) on OrbStack; docker ps -a / images / volumes / networks identical before and after. Full suite 1572 — 1557 pass, 15 skipped. — L1.8 review fixes (second pass): the snapshot's database must be published by a running container of the sandbox's own project made from its folder, and by no other project's container on any address (docker ps --filter publish); PostgresSnapshot and up's SELECT 1 connect to the published address (provider.address: 127.0.0.1), never to localhost — a URL naming an address is used as written (K2, K3).

items.requirement: Any segment (intro, outro, card, interstitial) can be a user video or image file (`intro: {video: assets/intro.mp4}`, `outro: {image: …, duration}`), with the theme transitions and audio rules applied; provided templates are never mandatory.
items.evidence: Scenario `intro` / `outro` / `card` / `interstitial` take `{video | image | lottie, from, to, fit, background, volume, duration}` (core types.ts MediaFileFields, schemas/primitives.ts mediaFileShape); a template's `components.intro / outro / interstitial` may be a file relative to the template folder (TemplateMediaRef, checkTemplateMedia) — no component is mandatory. They become uses of the built-in `studio/media` (video, image) / `studio/lottie` with the file in slot `file` (core media.ts mediaSegmentUse; components manifest `kinds` + `props.as`, registry usableAs). Positioned validation (core checks/media.ts): one file per use, extension per kind with hints (.gif, .lottie, a video given as image), existence, image signature, Lottie JSON, ffprobe (cached): unreadable / codec outside H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1, ProRes / non-WebM codec in .webm (errors), from / to past the end (error), part vs duration (warning), volume on a silent file (warning), no ffprobe (warning). Planner (editor plan.ts fileCandidate / useDuration, inputs.ts planInputFiles): the file's length (video part, Lottie) unless `duration`, note per use; the theme transitions around it (crossfade / fade-black measured on renders); audio: the file's own sound at `volume` (4-frame ramps at the part's edges, kit `filePartGain`, computed from the video element's own frame — review fix: the `volume` callback's frame restarted at 0 inside a transition's exiting window, replaying the start ramp mid-sound with a click and skipping the end ramp), a silent file stays silent, the music bed ducks under files with sound (frames.ts playsSound / duckSpans, musicVolumeAt); `fit: auto` (default) covers a file of about the frame's shape, else shows it whole (a 16:9 intro in the vertical variant). The render record says `audio: files | music+files`. Tests: core media.test.ts (9: validation messages and positions, probe parsing), components media.test.ts (kit helpers, kinds, fit auto, rendered as card / overlay), editor planner-media.test.ts (segments, theme file, durations, notes, ducking, vertical fit), render-media.test.ts (a real render: a 2 s intro and a 2 s outro video with their own tones, the intro leaving and the outro entering by the theme crossfade — per-frame RMS steady within 1 dB across the transition windows, the end ramp on the last frames; fails on the pre-fix callback; clips silent). A missing / unreadable file is a warning, shows nothing and is not a plan asset (review fix: it was registered and made the render refuse the plan; planner-media.test.ts checks plan.assets). Fixture scenario own-media (intro video with its own chime, outro image), run 20261012-093815-own-media: renders own-media-v6 (editorial + music; music ducked ≈ 6–7 dB under the intro's sound, not under the silent Lottie card or the image outro — measured on v2, same plan), own-media-v7 (motion: fade-black transitions), own-media-v8-vertical (intro and outro whole, fit auto; no music) — reviews clean. Intro audio measured after the review fix: in v8-vertical the intro's gain against assets/intro.mp4 (least squares per frame) is 1.000 on frames 3–104 and 0.68 / 0.49 / 0.25 on its last three frames (was 0.27 at frame 97 — the crossfade window — and 1.0 to the end in v5-vertical); v6 − v7 is bit-identical over the intro (the crossfade at frame 97 and the fade-black at 102 no longer change its sound); v6 vs v2 and v7 vs v3 differ only on frames 96–108 (pictures identical, PSNR ≥ 58 dB); the 3.22 s click (sample jump 0.0388) is gone (0.0037 = the source). L2.14 acceptance: own-media-v9 (run 20261012-093815-own-media, final engine, editorial + test bed) reviews clean, no visible change vs own-media-v6, audio music+files (docs/ACCEPTANCE-phase2.md).

items.evidence: Step `overlay: {video | image | lottie, at, anchor | rect, scale, fit, duration, loop, volume}` (core OverlaySpec, schemas/steps.ts; runner scenes.ts records it on the event with `at` and `box`). `at`: step / end (default), start, click, mark:<name>, seconds after the step start; `anchor`: target, cursor, screen, centre, the 8 sides / corners; `rect` in page CSS px; `scale` of the file's own size. items.requirement: The capture encodes during the take (screencast frames streamed to the encoder on the CFR schedule), so a take ends without a long encode and keeps no `frames/` by default; frames are kept only on request (raw export at the screencast's real timing); the edit stays frame-accurate (zooms, cursor sync, markers).

items.requirement: We sign the app, inside-out, with the hardened runtime on every Mach-O and the entitlements of one table (data + plists, the least an ad hoc probe proved) that must name every Mach-O of the payload (FAT included); dry builds are ad hoc and add only disable-library-validation where ad hoc needs it; bundle.json's hashes are the signed files'; the release path refuses before any tool runs unless the identity, the team and a notarisation credential that stays off every command line (a keychain profile or an API key file) are there, notarises the app as a zip then staples it, signs / notarises / staples the DMG and checks the team of every signature, Gatekeeper and both tickets, a failure's text naming no credential; every build verifies the result (deep strict verify, runtime, entitlements read back = the table, no get-task-allow, Resources byte for byte = the signed payload, no AppleDouble file or foreign extended attribute, Info.plist).

Gated acceptance after the review fixes, 2026-11-03 (RETAKE_TEST_BUNDLE=1, build inside the test with our ffmpeg, M4; 268 s, 6/6): build 108 s (stage 12.9 s, payload signing 4.8 s, tauri build 46.3 s, verification 16.6 s, DMG 26.8 s; a cold cargo cache ≈ 3 min); 35 signatures for 35 Mach-O files; 5 symbolic links kept; app 989 MB, DMG 425 MB (ULFO), payload 973 MB. From the built app only (PATH /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin, scratch HOME / RETAKE_HOME / TMPDIR; 143 canary packages — every bare specifier the engine's JavaScript names but does not hold — in 4 folders above the app and in the scratch home): `--version` names the app (directly and through a link), doctor 1.8 s with every tool `bundled` and Node.js = bundle.json's; `retake init`, then `run northfield-fixture quote` 50.1 s (25 steps) and `render --review --json` 83.4 s (1,823 frames, bundle 3.9 s, review clean, render browser `bundled`, no canary in the render bundle); the shell binary started directly (test mode, cwd outside the repository) served the Studio from `<Resources>/node/bin/node --require <Resources>/node/guard.cjs <Resources>/engine/dist/bin.js` in 0.8 s, the page redeemed its code, SIGTERM quit; a clone (cp -c) with canaries in Contents/node_modules and Retake.app/node_modules ran doctor (0 failures); afterwards no canary had run, bundle.json's sha256 values equalled the signed files, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` valid, nothing inside the app newer than the runs, ~/Library's entries for the bundle id unchanged (names, sizes, mtimes). L5.16e (the person's decision, 2026-11-04: releases from GitHub Actions; reworked after its two reviews): .github/workflows/release.yml on pushed v* tags, five jobs so that the signing keys never share a runner with dependency code (review e A-H1) — `release` (ubuntu, environment release: set-version --check, scripts/release.mjs tag, the tagged commit on main, `release.mjs preflight` — the Apple set, the updater set and the upload pair each all or nothing, a partial set failing before anything is built and naming each missing name and a name in the wrong store, seen only as `secrets.X != ''` —, a draft release); `build` (macos-15, contents: read, no secret, no variable, no environment: Node 22.16.0 checked against apps/desktop/bundle/node.json, frozen pnpm install, Rust 1.99.1 through rustup, the browsers checked against apps/desktop/bundle/browsers.json, our ffmpeg, `pnpm desktop:bundle --app-only`, packed with /usr/bin/tar and its sha256 as an output); `sign` (a fresh macos-15, environment release: the artifact's sha256 checked, then only `node apps/desktop/scripts/release.mjs sign` — whose whole import graph is Node.js built-ins and repository files — re-signing the ad hoc app inside-out with the Developer ID, notarising (notarytool --timeout, JSON, the log's issues on Invalid) and stapling, the update archive signed by the Tauri CLI checked file by file against tauri-cli.json and run from a fresh copy of those bytes, the DMG with hdiutil tried again on "Resource busy", Gatekeeper's words parsed); `attach` (refuses a public release, removes stale assets, uploads); `publish` (environment release: public, then the update from the release's archive — a missing one fails). The temporary keychain (ci-keychain.sh) imports the key non-extractable, gives every password to `security` on its standard input, and removes its files even when security fails. Every action pinned to the commit of an exact upstream tag (checkout v5.1.0, upload-artifact v6.0.0, download-artifact v6.0.0 — no setup or cache action since the hardening below; resolved read-only with gh api git/ref/tags). Proven on this Mac, 2026-11-04: `bundle.mjs build --app-only` 75 s (warm cargo), packed exactly as the build job does (tar.gz 368 MB, 23 s, sha256 checked, unpacked), then `release.mjs sign --tauri-cli … --app-version 0.2.0` with PATH /usr/bin:/bin and a scratch HOME: the Tauri CLI re-checked, the ad hoc app verified 3.6 s, DMG 431 MB made and verified 22 s; `--app-version 0.2.1` refused; the artifact's Tauri CLI signed a 0.3.0-rc.1 archive with a scratch key and the signature checked; then the gated bundle acceptance (desktop:bundle = layout + finishApp) 8/8 in 226 s (build 73 s, 35/35 signatures, app 990 MB, DMG 425 MB). L5.16f (the feed on a GitHub release): the upload pair is gone — two sets (`CONFIG_SETS`: apple, updater = the two TAURI_SIGNING secrets + the RETAKE_UPDATE_PUBKEY variable), the feed from GITHUB_SERVER_URL + GITHUB_REPOSITORY (`release.mjs feed`); `publish` binds no secret (the environment kept as the gate before going public), its Publish the update step gets the job token as GITHUB_TOKEN and the public key from the release job's output, one publish at a time across tags (job concurrency `release-publish`); no `UPDATES_*` name in the workflow. Hardening of the release tooling (2026-11-05): no cache and no setup action anywhere; every job's first step after its checkout is apps/desktop/scripts/ci-node.sh — the official node-v<version>-<platform>.tar.gz checked in the shell against apps/desktop/bundle/node.json's `tarballs` sha256 (the project's signed SHASUMS256.txt lines) before anything of it is unpacked or run, its bin/node against `sha256`, then first on PATH; package.json's packageManager carries pnpm's sha512. The sign job downloads and unpacks the build job's archive before any key is written: release.mjs unpack reads its members itself (`tarMembers`: ustar / pax, checksums, strict sizes, zeros after the end marker; GNU and sparse headers refused) and refuses any member but app/Retake.app and tauri-cli (the report no longer travels), an AppleDouble name, a hard link, a device, a fifo, a name given twice or a link out of the app, then tar extracts those very bytes (--no-mac-metadata --no-xattrs --no-acls --no-fflags) and every link of the app must resolve inside it by the system's realpath. The Tauri CLI runs from a fresh copy (`freshTauriCli`: each byte read checked again, O_NOFOLLOW, the copy checked last) made by finishApp right before the update archive is signed and removed right after, with HOME in the copy and refused when a folder of its module lookup path outside the copy exists (`cliLookupPaths`, equal to what Node.js reports); bundle.json's paths stay inside Resources; a reused stage of another version is refused before Tauri builds. items.requirement: A signed updater only in a build given a feed and a key: tauri-plugin-updater 2.14.0 behind the cargo `updater` feature, registered only when the build's config carries `plugins.updater` (pubkey, the one https feed, requireSignedVersion, no downgrade) — generated from RETAKE_UPDATE_FEED + RETAKE_UPDATE_PUBKEY (both or neither, checked) into the build's overlay, never committed, never `dangerous*` outside the gated test's own overlay; any other build says "Updates are off in this build". The update archive is ours (macOS tar: every link of the app, no AppleDouble entry or extended attribute, nothing outside the app) and signed by the pinned Tauri CLI bound to the app's version, the private key given to that one command only, the signature checked against the public key before the build ends.

items.requirement: The update flow: a check at launch at most once a day (remembered in the Retake home; RETAKE_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK turns it off) and Help › Check for Updates…; "Update available · vX" in the Studio's status bar opens a sheet with the release notes as text and Later · Install and Restart — nothing installs without that click, which no agent can make (own ops, never MCP tools). Install and Restart: refused from a translocated copy or a read-only disk and from a folder this account may not write; the archive downloaded and verified first (the key compiled in, the signed version); waits while a job of this workspace runs or waits; then a quit through the existing quit guard (unsaved text asks, page first), the owned server stopped gracefully, the bundle swapped, the app restarted (test mode: directly, never LaunchServices); a failed swap keeps the old app and says so. Doctor and Help show the date of the last successful check.

Processes still running from the old bundle (another workspace's worker, an MCP server) are not counted before the swap (BACKLOG BL-143); an admin install from a root-owned /Applications is not offered (BL-143). The non-test restart (Tauri's, through LaunchServices) and an install question left open past ten minutes run in no automated test: MACOS-CHECKLIST 15d steps 2–3. items.source: L5.16 plan §7 (release-feed), the person's choice: a static update feed of their own (L5.16d); the person's decision (2026-11-04): the feed on a GitHub release, no self-hosted host (L5.16f)
items.requirement: The release step publishes a signed update in a static feed on the repository's own GitHub releases (scripts/publish-update.mjs): nothing requested before the archive's minisign signature is verified in Node against the apps' public key (key id, Ed25519 over the BLAKE2b-512 prehash, the global signature over the trusted comment, its version equal to the one published); then, before any write, a public repository, the version's published release and what it holds being these very bits (never replaced, no override); the version's release only gains what it lacks (archive, .sig, platform-<platform>.json); the channels on one fixed `update-feed` release (created once, a pre-release never "latest"): rebuilt from the platform files (a re-run heals), rc.json for every version, latest.json for stable ones, never moved back, replaced through a temporary name so a channel is never half-written nor missing longer than one DELETE and the rename (each holder looked at again before its delete: a newer feed written meanwhile is kept; every request with a timeout, the idempotent ones asked again after a server error, a rate limit or a network error; a run that cannot rename keeps its temporary file and says the channel may be missing and to re-run); GitHub's REST API with GITHUB_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY only (GitHub's addresses by default, https only); release notes from the version's CHANGELOG paragraph (plain text) or --notes.

items.source: L5.14 plan 2 + critique 2 (the file queue: decision of 2026-11-04, no new dependency); BL-116; critique H2, M3, M5, H4
items.requirement: Heavy work not started waits while a filming take of the user holds (any workspace, the terminal included); a running heavy job yields during a take that starts after it — background QoS on its whole tree (the detached browser included), reversed per process after — chosen by a measured spike under today's render settings and BL-114's; a cancel while held ends the job in its own process (clean-ups run), its tree killed only after a grace period.
items.evidence: L5.14a: engine jobs/yield.ts (QosYield), the worker's heavy slot (yield.json while held). Spike on the M4 (fixture quote, 3 takes per condition, 5 alone): alone motion fps min median 60.3 (51.4–60.5), kicked 9, dropped 6, no stall; beside an untouched render 32.3 (today) / 28.9 (BL-114), kicked 16 / 19, stalls; render under background QoS 52.1 / 57.7, kicked 10 / 9, dropped 6 / 7, no stall; SIGSTOPped render 51.5 / 60.5. Both pass (≥ alone − max(2, spread 9.1)): QoS chosen (lower risk). Frames identical (today: 1832/1832) after QoS and SIGSTOP. Tests: packages/engine/test/yield.test.ts (ps -o pri 4 and back), packages/engine/test/worker-captures.test.ts ('a take starting mid-render: the whole tree (its browser too) at background priority, back after; identical frames', 'a cancel while held: the job process ends it itself (cancelled, nothing left under the render id), no kill'). L5.14a fixes: `-b` only on new pids of a held tree, each pid's QoS before the hold kept (a pid at background QoS before is never released to default), `ps` (5 s) and `taskpolicy` (10 s) with time limits (review A L3, L4, L5); every signal and every QoS root through one guard (jobs/signal.ts: never -1, 0, 1, the worker or its group: review B L1); the cancel-grace kill tested. DESIGN §4q lists every spike run: QoS passes today by 0.9 fps (52.1 against 51.2; one QoS take of three at 41.7), the 120 s stop failed 1 of 2 in both settings — L5.15 re-runs S4 for QoS. Tests: packages/engine/test/signal.test.ts ('never signals -1, 0, 1, a non-integer, this process or its own group — alone or as a tree'), packages/engine/test/yield.test.ts (new pids only, the QoS before kept, a hung ps), packages/engine/test/worker-heavy.test.ts ('a cancelled job process that ignores its cancel is killed cancelGraceMs later: cancelled (was killed)'), packages/engine/test/worker-captures.test.ts (10 runs in a row green). packages/engine/test/worker-heavy.test.ts ('review B L1: a job process that cannot start (no pid yet) is never signalled, even by a first signal right then; its job ends interrupted'); packages/engine/test/jobs.test.ts ('L5.14a fixes: a running job whose recorded worker pid is 0, 1 or -1 is derived interrupted (never a live worker)'). L5.14b measured acceptance from the Studio's own submits, 'packages/ui/test/captures-first-acceptance.test.ts' (RETAKE_TEST_CAPTURES_FIRST=1), run of 2026-11-04 15:37 on the M4: alone motion fps min 58.5 / 57.7 / 58.7, dropped 8 / 4 / 4, kicked 10; beside a render 57.7 / 58.6 / 56.5 (median 57.7 ≥ bar 56.5), dropped 4 / 6 / 10 (median 6, within the alone range 4–8; above the spike's +1), kicked 8 / 9 / 9, no freeze; takes started 245–375 ms after submit; the render at 6.1–6.5 frames/s during each take and 26.6–27.5 after; its job process tree at ps pri 4 during, back after; frames identical (framemd5 1816/1816 ×3). A later run under other sessions' load (load up to 31) failed on kicked (14 > 12): noise of the machine, the alone takes too (one at 26.9 fps). L5.14b fixes (review B M2, M3): the acceptance concludes only on a quiet machine (load at the start ≤ half the cores, each alone take's load ≤ 1.5 × the cores, alone motion fps within 10 fps, the spike's quiet alone spread being 9.1: else it fails "machine not quiet — re-run"), then fixed bars (every beside take ≥ the alone median − 2 fps; beside medians of dropped / kicked ≤ the alone takes' most), the render's speed before / during / after the take (after ≥ 0.8 × before; slower during asserted until L5.15, reported since — DESIGN §4q), and every process lowered to pri 4 back from it after (per pid). Run 3's numbers against these bars: lowest beside take 56.5 = the bar, dropped median 6 ≤ 8, kicked median 9 ≤ 10 (DESIGN §4q); not re-run after the change (see the gap).
items.gap: The acceptance with its final rule did not pass on the GPU path (2026-11-05, M4, quiet gate passed: start load 1.99): alone takes 58.6 / 58.7 / 58.7 fps min, dropped 4 / 4 / 4, kicked 10 / 9 / 10; beside a GPU render 57.6 / 57.7 / 55.1 (bar 56.7: the third take under it, its highest load 11.15 against 5.8–6.4 for the other two), dropped 4 / 7 / 5 (median 5 > the alone maximum 4), kicked 10 / 10 / 9; the render at 29.6–33.6 frames/s before, 6.3–6.8 during each take, 30.0–30.8 after (background QoS does slow a GPU render). An earlier run the same night: one beside take at 50 fps (numbers not kept). The bars were not widened; the person chose to commit L5.15 with this gap and re-run the acceptance later on an idle Mac (other sessions paused, the display awake).
